findings.claim: GetEqualityComparer<T>() previously threw TypeAccessException for any type with no known hash-resistant comparer, which is how MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData protects against hash-collision DoS. It now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default. Deserializing attacker-controlled keys into Dictionary/HashSet with an arbitrary key type under UntrustedData is therefore silently allowed with a non-resistant comparer. This removes the protection, and nothing in REQ-2129 calls for it.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a Dictionary<CustomKeyType,int> (CustomKeyType has a weak GetHashCode) with MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData). Base build throws TypeAccessException ("No hash-resistant equality comparer available"); head build succeeds. The existing MessagePackSecurityTests case that expects TypeAccessException for an unsupported key type should fail on head.
